classification.difficultyReason: Combine horizontal reflection, reciprocal dilation and translation with fractional coefficients and exact coordinate arithmetic.

content.prompt: Let $P(-2,y)$ lie on $y=f(x)$. Find the new $x$-coordinate of $P$ on each of the following.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=f\left(-\frac{1}{2}\left(x-\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)\end{align*}$$
Dilate horizontally by factor $2$, reflect in the $y$-axis, then translate right $\frac{1}{2}$ unit. The successive $x$-coordinates are
$$\begin{align*}x_1&=2(-2)=-4\\x_2&=-(-4)=4\\x_3&=4+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{9}{2}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}y&=f\left(-2\left(x-\frac{1}{8}\right)\right)\end{align*}$$
Dilate horizontally by factor $\frac{1}{2}$, reflect in the $y$-axis, then translate right $\frac{1}{8}$ unit. The successive $x$-coordinates are
$$\begin{align*}x_1&=\frac{1}{2}(-2)=-1\\x_2&=-(-1)=1\\x_3&=1+\frac{1}{8}=\frac{9}{8}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}y&=f\left(-\frac{2}{3}(x-2)\right)\end{align*}$$
Dilate horizontally by factor $\frac{3}{2}$, reflect in the $y$-axis, then translate right $2$ units. The successive $x$-coordinates are
$$\begin{align*}x_1&=\frac{3}{2}(-2)=-3\\x_2&=-(-3)=3\\x_3&=3+2=5\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}y&=f\left(-\frac{2}{3}(x-6)\right)\end{align*}$$
Dilate horizontally by factor $\frac{3}{2}$, reflect in the $y$-axis, then translate right $6$ units. The successive $x$-coordinates are
$$\begin{align*}x_1&=\frac{3}{2}(-2)=-3\\x_2&=-(-3)=3\\x_3&=3+6=9\end{align*}$$
